params.script_inline:
import sys, json

# The DECLARATION of this memory's own tool, in the hive, beside the cells that
# serve it.
#
# WHY IT LIVES HERE. Whoever is reached declares themselves. Until GH #552 this
# schema was a HAND-TYPED projection of THIS hive's own `in_query` contract,
# kept in a collector one composite away: `memory-hive` named seven context keys
# on that lane, three of them were the model's, and a person had retyped those
# three -- twice, because `talky`'s brain seeded a second copy -- into templates
# that answer no recall at all. Nothing but a test held the copies to the
# contract, and a schema held to its contract by a test is a schema that has no
# owner.
#
# The lane pair and the answer shape are the tools hive's, byte for byte
# (`templates/tools/README.md` § Asking for the declarations): a caller that can
# ask one answerer can ask the other, and the collector cuts three answers
# together without knowing which of them was a hive of tools.
#
# THE DESCRIPTION IS WHERE THE RULES ARE WRITTEN. `read_window` in `./recall`
# REFUSES a half-open window (`half_open_window`) rather than widening it, and
# until this cell existed that rule was enforced in one template and unsaid in
# another -- a model that named one bound bought a refusal it could not see
# coming. It is one sentence now, in the file that enforces it.
#
# THE TIER IS NOT AN ARGUMENT and never becomes one. How deep a recall runs is
# configuration of this hive (`./tool` params.tier); a model that could choose
# its own depth could ask for one the instance was tuned away from.
SCHEMAS = {
    "memory_recall": {
        "description":
            "Ask this member's long-term memory about something, optionally "
            "restricted to a time range. Name BOTH bounds or neither: a "
            "half-open window is refused, not widened.",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "query": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "what to look for"},
                "window_from": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "ISO-8601 start of the time range "
                                   "(optional; needs `window_to`)"},
                "window_to": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "ISO-8601 end of the time range "
                                   "(optional; needs `window_from`)"}},
            "required": ["query"]}}
}

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
body = doc["body"]
asked = body.get("tools")

# ABSENT and EMPTY are two different requests and must not look alike -- the
# same rule the tools hive follows. A caller that declared no tools gets no
# schemas, and that is an answer; a request that carries no `tools` slot at all
# lost it on the way.
if not isinstance(asked, list):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"operation": "schemas", "error_code": "tools_missing",
                   "schema_count": 0, "unknown_count": 0},
        "schemas": [], "unknown": [],
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": "the request carried no `tools` list"}]}))
    sys.exit(0)

names = [str(n) for n in asked if isinstance(n, str)]
if "*" in names:
    wanted, unknown = sorted(SCHEMAS), []
else:
    seen, wanted, unknown = set(), [], []
    for n in names:
        if n in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(n)
        (wanted if n in SCHEMAS else unknown).append(n)

schemas = [dict(name=n, **SCHEMAS[n]) for n in wanted]
header = {"operation": "schemas", "schema_count": len(schemas),
          "unknown_count": len(unknown)}
if unknown:
    # Named, never dropped: a caller asking this memory for a name it does not
    # serve has to learn that from the answer and not from a silence.
    header["error_code"] = "tool_unknown"
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
    "header": header, "schemas": schemas, "unknown": unknown, "messages": []}))

description.purpose: The declaration of this memory's OWN tool, handed out by name: a request naming `memory_recall` comes back as its JSON schema, and any other name comes back in `unknown` rather than as a silence. Whoever is reached declares themselves -- until GH #552 this schema was a HAND-TYPED projection of this hive's own `in_query` contract, living in a collector one composite away and seeded a second time into a brain, held to the contract by nothing but a test.
description.use_when: Reached on this hive's `in_schemas` lane, on an asking collector's menu tick, with the names that collector declares it uses. Never addressed by name, never part of a tool round: it answers no `tool_call` and carries no `tool_name`.
description.not_in_scope: No judgement about which tier a caller SHOULD ask for -- the tier is this hive's configuration (`./tool` params.tier) and deliberately not a model argument, because a model that could choose its own depth could ask for one the instance was tuned away from. No `thread_recall`: that one reads the COLLECTOR's own slate, which no other cell may read, so it is declared where it is answered. No provider envelope: the answer is {name, description, parameters}, and wrapping it in whatever a model provider wants is the caller's business.
description.emits_meaning: schemas[]: `{name, description, parameters}` for every asked name this hive serves, sorted for `*`. unknown[]: the names it does not serve, verbatim. hop.error_code `tool_unknown` when that list is non-empty, `tools_missing` when the request carried no `tools` slot at all -- an absent list and an empty one are two different requests.
description.consumes_meaning: body.tools: the names the asking collector declares it uses, e.g. ["memory_recall"]. The single entry ["*"] asks for everything this memory declares, which is one schema.
examples: {"tools":["memory_recall","web_search"]} -> one schema, unknown ["web_search"], hop.error_code `tool_unknown` -- the tools hive answers that one
